thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: metrics-log-ingest-lag (SEV2) —  Kafka consumer lag > 200k for topic=log-ingest-us-west
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: Alert assigned to oncall-sam — incident created: PD-4218
oncall-sam: acking and looking. noticed spikes in consumer lag + s3 429s earlier.
eng-lee: seeing prometheus scrape errors for node-exporter on k8s-pool-3 around 03:12 UTC. logs show many connection resets.
sre-maya: confirmed: kafka consumer group "log-ingest-consumers" lag ~268k, processing rate dropped to ~4k msg/s from 60k/s peak.
eng-lee: suspecting S3 throttling upstream causing write slowdowns to logstore, consumers backing up.
oncall-sam: running quick health checks. tailing consumer logs now. sharing snippet:

```
2026-03-15T03:14:22Z consumer[12]: ERROR: write to s3 failed: 503 SlowDown
2026-03-15T03:14:22Z consumer[12]: retrying batch 1/5
2026-03-15T03:15:03Z consumer[12]: commit failed: OffsetCommitError
```
infra-dana: any deploys in the last 30m to ingestion? I see a canary rollout for log-serializer at 02:58 UTC.
eng-lee: yes canary, but rollout paused automatically. telemetry shows latency increase correlating with s3 429s.
sre-maya: mitigation plan: 1) pause non-essential scrapers / reduce scrape frequency 2) scale consumers horizontally + increase consumer parallelism 3) throttle retries to avoid hot loops 4) open AWS support case for S3 429s
oncall-sam: doing (1) now: reducing Prometheus scrape targets to 60s for exporters in us-west and disabling some low-critical exporters.
oncall-sam: kubectl patch prometheusrule prometheus-prod --patch '{"spec":{"scrape_interval":"60s"}}' --namespace=monitoring
eng-lee: parallelizing consumers: bumping replicas for log-ingest-consumers to 12 -> 36

```
kubectl scale deployment/log-ingest-consumers -n prod --replicas=36
```
support-omar: paging support/next-level to prepare customer comms. which customers impacted most?
sre-maya: customers with high-volume ingestion older than 03:10 UTC likely to see 30-45m delay. affected orgs: org-nyc-ads, org-compliance-2 (partial). We'll prepare a targeted notify.
product-ivy: tagging this as potential compliance-impact — recommend sending an advisory to compliance contacts once we have ETA for backfill.
oncall-sam: AWS case opened (case #123456789) — they confirm service-side throttling in us-west-2; suggested wait + retry with exponential backoff. asked for request IDs.
eng-lee: doing controlled backfill: set consumer max_batch_size=500, retry_backoff_ms=5000 in the config via k8s configmap and rolling restart for consumers.

```
kubectl set env deploy/log-ingest-consumers -n prod MAX_BATCH_SIZE=500 RETRY_BACKOFF_MS=5000
kubectl rollout restart deploy/log-ingest-consumers -n prod
```
incident-bot: Note: PD escalation policy will trigger if unacked for 5m. oncall-sam acked earlier so no escalation.
oncall-sam: monitoring lag now — dropped from 268k -> 120k in 8 minutes after scaling and backoff changes.
sre-maya: also restarted exporter on k8s-pool-3 node-exporter-7f8c to fix scrape errors, prometheus targets started returning 200s.
eng-lee: consumer error rate decreased; processing rate up to ~38k msg/s.
support-omar: drafting customer message: short blurb + ETA for reprocessing. will wait until lag < 10k to send update.
infra-dana: heads-up — autoscaler hit quota on node pool. i'm manually provisioning 3 extra nodes to keep consumers healthy.
infra-dana: provisioned nodes and cordoned them for canary. should be available in ~4 minutes.
oncall-sam: follow-up: after node addition + consumer scaling, lag steady at ~7k and trending down. s3 429s are intermittent but not blocking writes.
product-ivy: any customer-visible errors (API 5xx) or is this only backend ingestion delay?
eng-lee: only backend ingestion delay. APIs are returning success; streaming ingestion is buffered. no query-side errors observed.
support-omar: sending targeted advisory to org-nyc-ads and org-compliance-2: "We're experiencing temporary log ingestion delays in us-west. We are mitigating — expected catch-up within 1 hour. We'll follow up when backfill is complete." getting signoff from infra-dana.
infra-dana: signoff, send it.
support-omar: sent.
eng-lee: monitoring consumer lag to zero. plan for next steps: 1) let backfill run to zero 2) restore original scrape intervals 3) run post-incident checks + postmortem
oncall-sam: setting a followup reminder and assigning postmortem to sre-maya and eng-lee.

```
/runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/log-ingest-backpressure
```
sre-maya: will capture timelines and config diffs. initial root cause likely transient S3 throttling + a canary that increased write pressure.
incident-bot: Incident updated: status=mitigating, severity=SEV2, owner=oncall-sam
oncall-sam: handing off to infra-dana for capacity cleanup and to eng-lee for postmortem writeup. I'm going offline for the next 30m, leave me a note if it re-escalates.
infra-dana: acknowledged handoff. will scale down extra nodes after backfill completes and run cost checks.
eng-lee: acknowledged. will ping when postmortem draft ready.
product-ivy: thanks all — keeping an eye on potential compliance fallout.
incident-bot: Incident resolved: metrics-log-ingest-lag cleared at 03:45 UTC. closing PD incident PD-4218.
oncall-sam: closing thread here. will add timeline to the postmortem and tag support/ops.
sre-maya: filing postmortem draft now.
support-omar: comms: "Backfill completed, customers processed; no data loss, only ingestion delay."
sre-maya: postmortem will include: timeline, root cause hypothesis, remediation (throttle retries, better canary controls, autoscaler quota alerts), and customer impact summary.
oncall-sam: great. thanks everyone for quick responses. :thumbsup:
